design_detail: News article in The BMJ (BMJ 2024;386:q1798, published 13 August 2024; one printed page with 7 references) by Elisabeth Mahase, on the retraction of three MDMA-assisted therapy papers by Psychopharmacology and the FDA's rejection of Lykos Therapeutics' new drug application. Sources cited: the three retraction notices (refs 1-3), a New York Times report (ref 4), a MAPS statement (ref 5), a CBC report (ref 6) and the final summary minutes of the FDA advisory committee meeting of 4 June 2024 (ref 7); company statements are quoted without references. The article has an unheaded opening section (5 paragraphs) and a section headed 'FDA rejects Lykos Therapeutics' application' (7 paragraphs). The PDF's second page is a permissions notice.
can_establish: What The BMJ reported on 13 August 2024 about the three retractions and the FDA decision, and which documents it relied on.
cannot_establish: What the FDA's own review found or why it decided as it did (its decision letter and review documents are not cited; the advisory committee minutes are summarized in one sentence without vote counts), or what the protocol violations were (the article relies on press reports for this).

sample.selection_effects: News selection: the sponsor's chief executive is quoted at length and the company's statements are relayed; no regulator, independent expert or author of the retracted papers is quoted.

analysis.effect_sizes: None. No vote counts are given for the advisory committee, and no date is given for the FDA decision.
analysis.selective_reporting: The article does not name the study site (the notices name it as the MP4 site), does not report that most of the authors who responded to the publisher disagreed with the retractions (as the notices record), and gives no source for its statement that the retracted research was not part of the application.

interpretation_gap.results_show: A dated news record: three retractions by Psychopharmacology for undisclosed protocol violations at one study site and incompletely declared competing interests; the FDA's rejection of the application, which came before the retractions; the advisory committee's majority views as summarized from its minutes; and the company's statements.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The headline joins the two events ('as FDA rejects'), but the text gives the journal's reasons for the retractions, which concern researchers' conduct at one site and undisclosed interests, not the FDA review, and says only that the retractions came after the decision. Its statement that the retracted research did not form part of the application is introduced with 'reports show' and has no source.

timeline.event: Lawsuit by a trial participant against an investigator at one study site, settled out of court, as reported by the article (citing a CBC report).
FDA Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting on 4 June 2024; final summary minutes dated 30 July 2024 (ref 7; not read).
FDA rejects Lykos Therapeutics' new drug application (date not given in the article; before the retractions).

Psychopharmacology retracts three phase 2 analyses (retraction notices by Feduccia et al., Jerome et al. and Mithoefer et al., 2024, published 10 August 2024; read in the app's browser by this reader).

replication.where_it_stands: The article's account of the retraction notices matches the notices themselves (checked by this reader on the publisher's pages). Its account of the FDA decision rests on the committee minutes, summarized without counts, and on the company's statements; the FDA's decision letter and review documents remain unread for this batch.

what_would_settle_it: The FDA's decision letter and review documents, and the advisory committee's briefing documents, transcript and vote counts, read in full; for the retractions, the sponsor's reanalysis of the phase 2 data without the MP4 site.

domains.note: A news report, not systematic; but its sources are named, including the primary notices and the committee minutes.
Its account of the notices matches them; the committee minutes are summarized in one sentence without counts, and the nature of the violations rests on press reports.

domains.domain: Reliance on the authors' own studies

domains.note: Statements are attributed to their sources, except that the retracted research was not part of the application; the headline implies a link between the two events that the text does not establish.

domains.domain: Balance of perspectives on the retractions and the FDA decision (the regulator's reasoning and the retracted papers' authors under-represented)
domains.note: The company is quoted at length; the regulator speaks only through the minutes; the authors' disagreement with the retractions, recorded in the notices, is not reported.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: No validated instrument applies to news reports (METHODS §5.3); the editors' narrative-review checklist is used. The article may be cited, as a news report, for the dated sequence of events and for what the committee minutes and the company said as it summarizes them; for the reasons for the retractions the notices themselves are the primary source, and for the FDA's reasons the agency's own documents are needed.

key_findings.finding: Three papers on MDMA-assisted psychotherapy were retracted by Psychopharmacology because of protocol violations amounting to unethical conduct by researchers at a study site (article published 13 August 2024).

According to the retraction notices (refs 1-3), the authors were aware of the violations when they submitted the articles but did not disclose them or remove the affected data from their analyses; all three papers related to phase 2 randomized controlled trials of MDMA-assisted therapy and had similar authors.

The notices did not say what the violations were; press reports (refs 4, 5) suggest that an investigator at one study site had an unethical sexual relationship with a trial participant; in a 2018 lawsuit settled out of court the participant said she had been sexually assaulted, and the investigator said the relationship was consensual (ref 6).

The journal said some authors had not fully declared competing interests, including that many were affiliated with MAPS or its subsidiary MAPS Public Benefit Corporation, now known as Lykos Therapeutics; MAPS fully funded the trials and provided the MDMA, and Lykos Therapeutics organised them.
key_findings.note: The notices themselves say 'two of the authors' (feduccia_2024) or 'several of the authors' (jerome_2024, mithoefer_2024); see reporting issue 3.

key_findings.finding: The retractions came after the US FDA rejected Lykos Therapeutics' new drug application for MDMA capsules for the treatment of PTSD; no date for the decision is given.
key_findings.locator: FDA rejects Lykos Therapeutics' application, 1st paragraph (left column)

key_findings.finding: According to the final summary minutes of the FDA Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting of 4 June 2024 (ref 7, dated 30 July 2024), most committee members did not believe the available data showed the drug was effective in people with PTSD, and all but one said its benefits did not outweigh its risks. No vote counts are given.
key_findings.locator: FDA rejects Lykos Therapeutics' application, 2nd paragraph (left column); reference 7

key_findings.finding: According to Lykos Therapeutics, the FDA asked for another phase 3 trial to give better evidence on safety and efficacy; the company said it would request a meeting to ask for reconsideration and to discuss a resubmission for midomafetamine (MDMA) capsules.
key_findings.locator: FDA rejects Lykos Therapeutics' application, 3rd and 4th paragraphs (left column, continued in the right column)

key_findings.finding: The company's chief executive, Amy Emerson, who sits on the MAPS board, said another phase 3 study would take several years and that many of the requests could be met with existing data, post-approval requirements or the scientific literature; the article notes that Emerson was an author on two of the retracted papers.
key_findings.locator: FDA rejects Lykos Therapeutics' application, 5th and 6th paragraphs (right column)

key_findings.finding: The article states that reports show the research in the three retracted papers did not form part of the company's FDA application; no source is given.
key_findings.locator: FDA rejects Lykos Therapeutics' application, 7th paragraph (right column)

key_findings.finding: The retraction notices are cited as Feduccia et al. (doi 10.1007/s00213-024-06671-0, PMID 39126502), Jerome et al. (doi 10.1007/s00213-024-06665-y, PMID 39126500) and Mithoefer et al. (doi 10.1007/s00213-024-06666-x, PMID 39126501), all Psychopharmacology 2024.

reporting_issues.issue: Reference 5 names the organisation the 'Multidisciplinary Association for Psychedelic Substances'; the text, and the retraction notices, name it the Multidisciplinary Association for Psychedelic Studies.
reporting_issues.consequence: Typographical; use the name given in the text.

reporting_issues.issue: The statement that the retracted research did not form part of the FDA application is introduced with 'reports show' and has no reference.
reporting_issues.consequence: Not citable as established; the application's contents would have to be checked in the regulator's documents.

reporting_issues.issue: The article says the journal noted that many of the authors were affiliated with MAPS or MAPS PBC; the notices say 'two of the authors' for one paper and 'several of the authors' for the other two (checked by this reader on the publisher's pages).
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor; cite the notices for the wording.

reporting_issues.issue: The article does not give the date of the FDA decision, the committee's vote counts, the name of the study site (MP4 in the notices) or the fact, recorded in the notices, that most of the authors who responded to the publisher disagreed with the retractions.
reporting_issues.consequence: These details must come from the notices and the regulator's documents.

verification.source_read: PDF p. 1 (PDFs/MDMA/Mahase_2024_ThreePapersRetractedFDA.pdf): the one-page news article read in full, including its seven references, and the page rendered; the PDF's second page is a permissions notice. Compared with the three retraction notices, read on the publisher's pages in the app's browser on the same day.
